games.summary: hachico wins with Devastating Blow and Feu Awakening.

beats.text: Creative Tinder and Liminal Guide build hachico’s opening hand.
Judges catch the missing Angelic Channeling draw; the casters describe an easy correction.
Dungeon Guide advances Ciel to level 3 before Devastating Blow applies pressure.
Manxome Armoire retrieves Devastating Blow; wenwen releases the spirit and uses healing herbs, but Feu Awakening closes the game.

games.summary: hachico wins through the attempted counter and spirit release.

beats.text: Two Gentle Respites give wenwen a stronger start.
Beguiling Coup brings Devastating Blow into the attack, pushing wenwen to 14 damage counters.
Feu Awakening stops the attempted negate; wenwen releases the spirit before Devastating Blow resolves.
Ciel’s end-step damage finishes wenwen; the casters clarify another Feu Awakening is unnecessary.

match.sourceNote: Reviewed sequentially from the Osaka Day 1 machine transcript. Both game finishes are narrated; official round 1 pairing confirms hachico 2–0. Damage-counter figures are not life totals.

games.summary: Professor wins; only the closing position is transcribed.

beats.text: Poitier arrives as a large ally, and Danriick concedes. The earlier game is absent from this transcript.

games.summary: Professor’s Umbra allies force the concession.

beats.text: Professor advances Alice to level 2 and sets up Umbra Sight.
Infernal Vessel threatens the healing plan; Fiery Interference answers the lineage release.
Beseech the Winds enables the climb to Vanitas level 3, but Imperial Countermeasure stops the attacks.
Nocturne’s Oblivion removes Infernal Vessel; Remnant of Will restores the healing plan.
Poitier and Argus establish the board Danriick cannot break; Professor takes the match.

match.sourceNote: Partial round 2 coverage: source jumps from the round 1 interview at 1:30:19 to the end of game 1 at 2:30:00. Game 2 is narrated continuously; official pairing confirms Professor 2–0. No unseen opening sequence reconstructed.

beats.text: Dream Fairy returns Aquifer Seneschal to memory; Luster’s Shroud preserves the lock.
Dream Fairy returns Tweedledee, and Rowland helps clear Jueying.
Augustine converts Manxome Armoire into a fractal, giving Xenadrael the resources for Frozen Dismissal against Guan Yu.
The rebuilt ally board pushes damage and closes game 1.

games.summary: Mono protects Liu Bei and Dilu to even the match.

beats.text: After the Avatar is dismissed, Virgil and Liu Bei remove Lucca.
Dilu removes Portly Raccoon, and Mortal Ambition turns the attempted attack into retaliation.
Luster’s Shroud preserves Liu Bei against Bandit; Cyclonic Fatestone later suppresses Jueying.
Mono attacks through Tariff Ring with Dilu and Liu Bei for the last five damage.

games.summary: Xenadrael wins the race with allies after Mortal Ambition kills the raccoon.

beats.text: Xenadrael shifts toward direct pressure with Heavy Swing rather than trading into Liu Bei.
Purifying Thurible removes Heavy Swing before it can become an Omen.
Veiling Breeze stops the sword attack, and Guo Jia enables Fabled Emerald Fatestone.
Mortal Ambition answers the raccoon’s attack and kills the raccoon; it does not damage Xenadrael’s champion.
Nia and Jueying provide the final attacks, overcoming Mono’s remaining defenses.

match.sourceNote: All three games reviewed sequentially. Earlier Water D speculation is superseded by Ciel level 1 and the official list. The casters’ hypothetical Mortal Ambition champion-lethal line does not occur: the raccoon takes retaliation, then Nia and Jueying finish Mono. Official round 3 pairing confirms Xenadrael 2–1.
